purpose: Original synthetic engineering paragraphs; not a capability benchmark, replay corpus, or sealed evaluation.
rows: In this invented workshop, a blue tray holds three wooden tokens. Mira moves one token to an empty green tray. The blue tray then holds two tokens, and the green tray holds one token.
The fictional station has two clocks. Clock A marks the start of a shift. Clock B marks its end. A note made between these two events belongs to that shift, not to the next one.
A small catalog labels a copper box as item seven. The box contains a paper star. Replacing the box label does not replace the star stored inside it.
In a made-up garden, the east gate opens before the west gate. The caretaker records each opening on a separate line. The first recorded opening belongs to the east gate.
A pretend robot follows a written rule: read the card, move the marked bead, then place the card face down. The face-down card shows that its instruction has already been used.
Four fictional books sit on a shelf. The red book is left of the gray book. The gray book is left of the white book. These statements describe order, not the number of pages.
The exercise defines a symbol named lum as a container, not a number. A description of a lum may list its contents. No other meaning of this invented symbol is assumed.
A practice log separates observations from guesses. An observation says that a lamp is off. It does not say whether the battery is empty, because the log provides no test of the battery.
